questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Import NYC_Film_Permits.txt into Excel. How many records (data rows, not counting the header) does the table have?

fields.label: Number of records
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film

questions.steps: Data → From Text/CSV (comma delimiter, file origin UTF-8). Check the row count in the status bar or with =ROWS(Table1).

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many columns does the imported permit table have?

fields.label: Number of columns
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('film')

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many records have a missing value for ZipCode? (Missing values are recorded as N/A.)

fields.label: Records with missing ZipCode
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE ZipCode = 'N/A'

questions.steps: =COUNTIF(N:N,"N/A")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 3

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many records have a ZipCode that is present but invalid (not a five-digit number)?

fields.label: Records with an invalid ZipCode
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE ZipCode <> 'N/A' AND (length(ZipCode) <> 5 OR ZipCode GLOB '*[^0-9]*')

questions.steps: Add a helper column =LEN([@ZipCode]) and filter for values other than 5, excluding N/A.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 4

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which column has the same value for every record? Give the exact column name.

fields.label: Column name
fields.method: SELECT 'EventAgency'

questions.steps: Use a pivot table or =COUNTA(UNIQUE(col)) per column; the one with a single distinct value is constant.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 5

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What are the oldest and newest EnteredOn values? Give the complete date and time.

fields.label: Oldest EnteredOn
fields.method: SELECT MIN(EnteredOn) FROM film

fields.label: Newest EnteredOn
fields.method: SELECT MAX(EnteredOn) FROM film

questions.steps: =MIN(E:E) and =MAX(E:E), formatted as date-time. If the dates are text, the import used the wrong locale.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 6 and 7

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many different event types are there, and which is the most common?

fields.label: Number of event types
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT EventType) FROM film

fields.label: Most common event type
fields.method: SELECT EventType FROM film GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 8 and 9

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits were granted for student films?

fields.label: Student-film shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Category = 'Student'

questions.steps: =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",K:K,"Student")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 11

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What percentage of shooting permits required approval by more than one Community Board? (A permit lists several boards separated by commas.)

fields.label: Share of shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT AVG(CommunityBoards LIKE '%,%') FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",I:I,"*,*")/COUNTIF(B:B,"Shooting Permit")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 12

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: In which year(s) did the number of shooting permits starting in Brooklyn exceed those starting in Manhattan? List every year where this holds.

fields.label: Year(s)
fields.method: SELECT group_concat(y, ', ') FROM (SELECT substr(StartDateTime,1,4) y FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 HAVING SUM(Borough='Brooklyn') > SUM(Borough='Manhattan') ORDER BY 1)

questions.steps: Pivot table: rows = YEAR(StartDateTime), columns = Borough, values = count, filtered to shooting permits.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 13
instructor.note: Brooklyn also exceeds Manhattan in 2018 (176 vs 138), but the data ends on 9 February 2018, so 2018 is a partial year. The key gives 2017 only, which is correct if partial years are excluded. The question does not say so.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What share of shooting permits in Manhattan take place on or near Broadway (BROADWAY appears anywhere in ParkingHeld)? Round to the nearest percent.

fields.label: Share (nearest percent)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(upper(ParkingHeld) LIKE '%BROADWAY%'),2) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Borough='Manhattan'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 14

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits entered since 1 January 2013 are for a country other than the United States of America?

fields.label: Foreign shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Country <> 'United States of America' AND EnteredOn >= '2013-01-01'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 15

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is the average duration of a shooting permit in hours? Round to the nearest half hour.

fields.label: Average duration (hours)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG((julianday(EndDateTime)-julianday(StartDateTime))*24)*2)/2 FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: Helper column =(D2-C2)*24, then =MROUND(AVERAGEIF(B:B,"Shooting Permit",helper),0.5).

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 16

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What was the duration of the shortest shooting permit, in minutes?

fields.label: Shortest duration (minutes)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(MIN((julianday(EndDateTime)-julianday(StartDateTime))*24*60)) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 17

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is the average lead time in days between EnteredOn and StartDateTime for shooting permits? Round to the nearest day.

fields.label: Average lead time (days)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(StartDateTime)-julianday(EnteredOn))) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 18

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: On which day of the week do most shooting permits start? Give the full day name.

fields.label: Day of week
fields.method: SELECT CASE strftime('%w',StartDateTime) WHEN '0' THEN 'Sunday' WHEN '1' THEN 'Monday' WHEN '2' THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN '3' THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN '4' THEN 'Thursday' WHEN '5' THEN 'Friday' ELSE 'Saturday' END FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

questions.steps: =TEXT(C2,"dddd") in a helper column, then a pivot table count.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 19

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What percentage of shooting permits include shooting on at least part of a Friday? Round to two decimal places of a percent.

fields.label: Share of shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT AVG(strftime('%w',StartDateTime)='5' OR strftime('%w',EndDateTime)='5' OR (julianday(date(EndDateTime))-julianday(date(StartDateTime))) >= ((5-CAST(strftime('%w',StartDateTime) AS INT)+7)%7)) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: A permit touches a Friday if it starts or ends on one, or spans enough days to pass one: compare the day count with the days from the start weekday to the next Friday.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 20

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Split EmployeeCode into Location, EmpID, PlantID and PayPeriod. How many employees work in the USA, and how many of them are paid weekly?

fields.label: Employees in USA
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='USA'

fields.label: …paid weekly
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='USA' AND substr(EmployeeCode,-1)='W'

questions.steps: Location =LEFT(A2,3); PayPeriod =RIGHT(A2,1); then COUNTIFS.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Create LocationPlantID (for example USA-12). How many distinct LocationPlantID values are there?

fields.label: Distinct LocationPlantID values
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT)) FROM codes2

questions.steps: =LEFT(A2,3)&"-"&MID(A2,FIND("-",A2)+1,LEN(A2)-FIND("-",A2)-1), then =COUNTA(UNIQUE(range)).

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which LocationPlantID has the most employees, and how many?

fields.label: LocationPlantID
fields.method: SELECT substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT) FROM codes2 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1

fields.label: Employees
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 GROUP BY substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT) ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Extract EmpID with MID. What is the sum of all EmpID values, and how many employees have an EmpID above 1500?

fields.label: Sum of EmpID
fields.method: SELECT SUM(CAST(substr(EmployeeCode,4,4) AS INT)) FROM codes2

fields.label: EmpID above 1500
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE CAST(substr(EmployeeCode,4,4) AS INT) > 1500

questions.steps: =VALUE(MID(A2,4,4)). The sum works as a hash total: if any EmpID was extracted wrongly, it will not reconcile.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is the highest PlantID used in Germany (GER), and how many German employees are paid monthly?

fields.label: Highest PlantID in GER
fields.method: SELECT MAX(CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT)) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='GER'

fields.label: GER employees paid monthly
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='GER' AND substr(EmployeeCode,-1)='M'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Create a column showing "Plant 10–14" for PlantID 10 to 14 and "Plant 15+" otherwise. How many employees fall in "Plant 15+"?

fields.label: Employees in Plant 15+
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT) >= 15

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Build the flat file (Case 4 solution). As control totals: how many journal lines are there, and what is the total of the Debit column?

fields.label: Journal lines
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines

fields.label: Total Debit
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Debit<>'' THEN Debit END),2) FROM je_lines

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Do the journal lines balance? Give the sum of the Amount column (debits positive, credits negative).

fields.label: Sum of Amount
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Amount),2) FROM je_lines

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add AccountType with INDEX/MATCH. What is the total Amount on lines whose AccountType is Revenue?

fields.label: Total Amount, Revenue accounts
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Amount),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE a.AccountType LIKE 'Revenue%'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add BusinessUnit to each line. Which business unit has the most journal lines, and how many?

fields.label: Business unit
fields.method: SELECT b.BusinessUnit FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Journal lines
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID GROUP BY b.BusinessUnit ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: PreparerID is only unique together with BusinessUnitID. Add PreparerName using both keys. How many journal lines were prepared by Carolyn Slater?

fields.label: Lines prepared by Carolyn Slater
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE p.PreparerName LIKE 'Carolyn Slater%'

questions.steps: Match on a concatenated key: =INDEX(PreparerInfo!A:A,MATCH(D2&"|"&C2,PreparerInfo!B:B&"|"&PreparerInfo!C:C,0)). A match on PreparerID alone picks the wrong person.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many journal lines have no matching preparer in PreparerInfo (for example lines entered by a subsystem)?

fields.label: Lines without a preparer
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE p.PreparerName IS NULL

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add Source to each line. What is the total Debit for lines with Source = CHECK?

fields.label: Total Debit, CHECK
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.Debit<>'' THEN l.Debit END),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE s.Source='CHECK'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add GLAccountName. Which GL account has the largest total Debit, and what is that total?

fields.label: GL account name
fields.method: SELECT trim(a.GLAccountName) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE l.Debit<>'' GROUP BY a.GLAccountName ORDER BY SUM(l.Debit) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Total Debit
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Debit),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE l.Debit<>'' GROUP BY a.GLAccountName ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Using AccountClass, what is the total Amount booked to Cash accounts?

fields.label: Total Amount, Cash class
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Amount),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE a.AccountClass='Cash'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many distinct journal entries (JENumber) are in the file, and how many lines does the largest entry have?

fields.label: Distinct journal entries
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT JENumber) FROM je_lines

fields.label: Lines in the largest entry
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines GROUP BY JENumber ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Import both payroll files (they are pipe-delimited). As control totals, how many rows does each file have?

fields.label: Rows in 2015 file
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pay15

fields.label: Rows in 2016 file
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pay16

questions.steps: Data → From Text/CSV, set the delimiter to | (Custom). Opening the file directly puts everything in column A.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is total gross pay for January–June 2015 (Reg_Pay + OT_Pay) and for January–June 2016 (Gross_Wages)?

fields.label: Gross pay 2015
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay)),2) FROM pay15

fields.label: Gross pay 2016
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Gross_Wages),2) FROM pay16

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Noah says payroll rose by about $266,000. What is the exact difference in gross pay (2016 minus 2015)?

fields.label: Difference (2016 − 2015)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND((SELECT SUM(Gross_Wages) FROM pay16) - (SELECT SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay)) FROM pay15),2)

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Extract the three-digit job code from Job (2015) and Project (2016). Which job code has the largest 2016 gross wages, and how much?

fields.label: Job code
fields.method: SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END FROM pay16 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY SUM(Gross_Wages) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Gross wages 2016
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Gross_Wages),2) FROM pay16 GROUP BY CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.steps: =IF(ISNUMBER(VALUE(MID(A2,3,1))),MID(A2,3,3),MID(A2,4,3)) — keep it as text so 001 does not become 1.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: For job code 005 (Installation), what were total hours (regular + overtime) in 2015 and in 2016?

fields.label: Hours 2015
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Reg_Hrs+OT_Hrs),2) FROM pay15 WHERE CASE WHEN substr(Job,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Job,4,3) ELSE substr(Job,3,3) END='005'

fields.label: Hours 2016
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Hours+OT_Hours),2) FROM pay16 WHERE CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END='005'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which job code has the largest increase in gross pay from 2015 to 2016, and what is the increase?

fields.label: Job code
fields.method: SELECT j FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END j, SUM(Gross_Wages) g FROM pay16 GROUP BY 1) a JOIN (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Job,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Job,4,3) ELSE substr(Job,3,3) END j, SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay)) g FROM pay15 GROUP BY 1) b USING(j) ORDER BY a.g-b.g DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Increase
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(a.g-b.g,2) FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END j, SUM(Gross_Wages) g FROM pay16 GROUP BY 1) a JOIN (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Job,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Job,4,3) ELSE substr(Job,3,3) END j, SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay)) g FROM pay15 GROUP BY 1) b USING(j) ORDER BY a.g-b.g DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What was the average gross pay per hour (gross pay ÷ regular + overtime hours) in 2015 and in 2016? Two decimals.

fields.label: Per hour 2015
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay))/SUM(Reg_Hrs+OT_Hrs),2) FROM pay15

fields.label: Per hour 2016
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Gross_Wages)/SUM(Hours+OT_Hours),2) FROM pay16

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many 2015 rows have a job code outside the valid range 001–012?

fields.label: Rows with invalid job code
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pay15 WHERE CASE WHEN substr(Job,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Job,4,3) ELSE substr(Job,3,3) END NOT IN (SELECT Job_Code FROM jobcodes)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: An album counts as downloaded when all of its tracks are on a single invoice. How many distinct albums have been downloaded?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT x.AlbumId) FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId, t.AlbumId, COUNT(DISTINCT il.TrackId) n
         FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY 1, 2) x
       JOIN (SELECT AlbumId, COUNT(*) n FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId) a ON a.AlbumId = x.AlbumId WHERE x.n = a.n

instructor.source: PWC answers.docx (SQL Part 1 instructor key), question 22
instructor.note: 49 is the number of invoice–album pairs where the whole album was bought; those 49 purchases cover 41 different albums. Every one of them is a single-track album. The question asks for distinct albums, which is 41.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits last longer than one week (more than 168 hours)? Such long permits are worth checking with the issuing agency.

fields.label: Shooting permits over 168 hours
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND (julianday(EndDateTime) - julianday(StartDateTime)) * 24 > 168

questions.steps: Helper column =(D2-C2)*24, then =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",helper,">168").

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits were entered into the system after the shoot had already started?

fields.label: Shooting permits entered late
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND EnteredOn > StartDateTime

questions.steps: =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",helper,"<0") with helper =C2-E2.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many different valid ZipCode values appear in the file (ignore N/A)?

fields.label: Distinct ZipCodes
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ZipCode) FROM film WHERE ZipCode <> 'N/A'

questions.steps: =COUNTA(UNIQUE(FILTER(N2:N33503,N2:N33503<>"N/A"))).

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits run past midnight (end on a later calendar day than they start), and what share of all shooting permits is that?

fields.label: Overnight shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND date(EndDateTime) > date(StartDateTime)

fields.label: Share of shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT AVG(date(EndDateTime) > date(StartDateTime)) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: Compare =INT(D2) with =INT(C2): INT strips the time and leaves the date serial.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Across all years, in which calendar month do the most shooting permits start (1–12), and how many start in that month?

fields.label: Month
fields.method: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', StartDateTime) AS INT) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY strftime('%m', StartDateTime) ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.steps: Helper column =MONTH(C2), then a pivot table count.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: On average, how many community boards does a shooting permit list? Count the comma-separated values in CommunityBoards; two decimals.

fields.label: Average boards per permit
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(length(CommunityBoards) - length(replace(CommunityBoards, ',', '')) + 1), 2) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: =LEN(I2)-LEN(SUBSTITUTE(I2,",",""))+1 counts the items in each cell.

questions.subject: Excel

fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG((julianday(EndDateTime) - julianday(StartDateTime)) * 24), 1) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY Category ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: At which hour of the day (0–23) do the most shooting permits start, and how many start in that hour?

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Half of all shooting permits are applied for less than how many days ahead of the shoot? Compute the median of StartDateTime − EnteredOn (one decimal) and explain why it differs from the mean.

fields.label: Median lead time (days)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(x), 1) FROM (SELECT x FROM (SELECT (julianday(StartDateTime) - julianday(EnteredOn)) x FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit') ORDER BY x LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit') % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit') - 1) / 2)

questions.steps: =MEDIAN(IF(B2:B33503="Shooting Permit",C2:C33503-E2:E33503)). A median below the mean means a few very early applications pull the mean up.

questions.prompt: What is the total Credit for the HOTEL business unit? Give it as a negative number.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which valid job codes (001–012) have hours in 2016 but no hours at all in 2015? List them. Why does this matter for explaining the payroll increase?

fields.label: Job code(s)
fields.method: SELECT group_concat(j, ', ') FROM (SELECT Job_Code j FROM jobcodes WHERE Job_Code IN (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END FROM pay16 WHERE Hours + OT_Hours > 0) AND Job_Code NOT IN (SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Job,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Job,4,3) ELSE substr(Job,3,3) END FROM pay15 WHERE Reg_Hrs + OT_Hrs > 0) ORDER BY 1)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Which cardholders had three or more 2014 transactions between $4,500.00 and $4,999.99? Show name and number of such transactions, most first.
questions.sql:
SELECT FullName, COUNT(*) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount BETWEEN 4500 AND 4999.99
        GROUP BY FullName HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Walmart appears under several vendor names (WAL-MART #…, WM SUPERCENTER…, WALMART.COM…). What was total 2014 spending at all Walmart variants? Two decimals.
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND (upper(Vendor) LIKE 'WAL-MART%' OR upper(Vendor) LIKE 'WALMART%' OR upper(Vendor) LIKE 'WM SUPERCENTER%')

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many cardholders made at least one purchase in every month of 2014?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT FullName FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > 0 GROUP BY FullName HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Month) = 12)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: What share of 2014 positive spending went to the ten vendors with the most positive spending? Percent, two decimals.
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT SUM(t) FROM (SELECT SUM(Amount) t FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > 0 GROUP BY Vendor ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 10))
        / SUM(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > 0

columns:
ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT SUM(t) FROM (SELECT SUM(Amount) t FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > 0 GROUP BY Vendor ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 10))
        / SUM(Amount), 2)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many cardholders appear in 2014 but not in 2013?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT FullName FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 EXCEPT SELECT FullName FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2013)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Among MCCs with at least 100 transactions in 2014, show the five with the highest average transaction: MCC, number of transactions and average (two decimals).
questions.sql:
SELECT MCC, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 GROUP BY MCC HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
        ORDER BY AVG(Amount) DESC LIMIT 5

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Compare December spending: show the year and total amount (two decimals) for December 2013 and December 2014.
questions.sql: SELECT Year, ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Month = 12 GROUP BY Year

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many 2014 transactions have a missing Description, or a Description of just '0'?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND (Description IS NULL OR trim(Description) IN ('', '0'))

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Show cardholders with at least $10,000 of 2014 purchases whose 2014 refunds exceed 10% of those purchases: name, purchases and refunds (refunds as a positive number), both two decimals.
questions.sql:
SELECT FullName, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Amount > 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 2), ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN Amount < 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 2)
        FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 GROUP BY FullName
        HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN Amount > 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END) >= 10000
           AND -SUM(CASE WHEN Amount < 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END) > 0.1 * SUM(CASE WHEN Amount > 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END)

columns: ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Amount > 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 2)
ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN Amount < 0 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 2)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many distinct vendors were used in 2014, and how many of them appear in only one 2014 transaction?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(n = 1) FROM (SELECT Vendor, COUNT(*) n FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 GROUP BY Vendor)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Show 2014 activity per quarter: quarter (1–4), number of transactions and total amount (two decimals), first quarter first.
questions.sql: SELECT (Month + 2) / 3 AS Quarter, COUNT(*), ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 GROUP BY Quarter ORDER BY Quarter

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Which cardholder received the largest single refund in 2014? Show the name, the amount and the vendor.
questions.sql: SELECT FullName, Amount, Vendor FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 ORDER BY Amount LIMIT 1

questions.prompt: Show the description of the crime reported on Chamberlin Street on 28 July 2020.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many ATM withdrawals were made on Fifer Street on 28 July 2020, and what was their total amount?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM atm_transactions WHERE year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 28 AND atm_location = 'Fifer Street' AND transaction_type = 'withdraw'

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: List the license plates of cars that left the courthouse between 10:15 and 10:25 on 28 July 2020.
questions.sql: SELECT license_plate FROM courthouse_security_logs WHERE year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 28 AND activity = 'exit' AND hour = 10 AND minute BETWEEN 15 AND 25

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many phone calls on 28 July 2020 lasted less than one minute?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM phone_calls WHERE year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 28 AND duration < 60

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: What is the earliest flight out of Fiftyville on 29 July 2020? Show the destination city, hour and minute.
questions.sql:
SELECT a.city, f.hour, f.minute FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON a.id = f.destination_airport_id
       WHERE f.origin_airport_id = (SELECT id FROM airports WHERE city = 'Fiftyville') AND f.year = 2020 AND f.month = 7 AND f.day = 29
       ORDER BY f.hour, f.minute LIMIT 1

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many passengers were on the earliest flight out of Fiftyville on 29 July 2020?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM passengers WHERE flight_id = (SELECT id FROM flights WHERE origin_airport_id = (SELECT id FROM airports WHERE city = 'Fiftyville')
       AND year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 29 ORDER BY hour, minute LIMIT 1)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: List the names of people who left the courthouse by car between 10:15 and 10:25 on 28 July 2020 and also withdrew money on Fifer Street that day.
questions.sql:
SELECT p.name FROM people p
        WHERE p.license_plate IN (SELECT license_plate FROM courthouse_security_logs WHERE year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 28 AND activity = 'exit' AND hour = 10 AND minute BETWEEN 15 AND 25)
          AND p.id IN (SELECT b.person_id FROM bank_accounts b JOIN atm_transactions t ON t.account_number = b.account_number
                       WHERE t.year = 2020 AND t.month = 7 AND t.day = 28 AND t.atm_location = 'Fifer Street' AND t.transaction_type = 'withdraw')

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many flights left Fiftyville in total, and to how many different destination cities?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT destination_airport_id) FROM flights
       WHERE origin_airport_id = (SELECT id FROM airports WHERE city = 'Fiftyville')

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Show each ATM location and the total amount withdrawn there on 28 July 2020, largest first.
questions.sql: SELECT atm_location, SUM(amount) FROM atm_transactions WHERE year = 2020 AND month = 7 AND day = 28 AND transaction_type = 'withdraw' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Who made the most phone calls (as caller) in the data? Show the name and the number of calls.
questions.sql: SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) FROM phone_calls c JOIN people p ON p.phone_number = c.caller GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
